title: Client keepalive stops sending pings after 2 attempts
body:
### What version of gRPC and what language are you using?

Python 1.36.1


### What operating system (Linux, Windows,...) and version?

Linux Debian 10.8

### What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g. python version or version of gcc)

Python 3.7.3


### What did you do?

1. Configure client keepalives with a very short time `('grpc.keepalive_time_ms', 500)`.
2. Make an RPC to a server that hangs for 60 seconds.


### What did you expect to see?

* This client should ping every 10 seconds (As [recommended by the Client Keepalives design doc](https://github.com/grpc/proposal/blob/master/A8-client-side-keepalive.md#extending-for-basic-health-checking): "KEEPALIVE_TIME, defaulting to infinite. If smaller than ten seconds, ten seconds will be used instead."
* After pinging a few times, the server should close the channel with GOAWAY too_many_pings


### What did you see instead?

* Client writes the request and a PING_RESPONSE
* +500 ms: sends a keepalive ping
* +500 ms: TRIES to send a ping, but there is a 1s minimum so it reschedules it
* +500 ms: sends a second keepalive ping
* +500 ms: `CLIENT: Ping delayed [ipv4:127.0.0.1:8001]: too many recent pings: 0/2` ; it never sends a ping again
* +58 s: the response is received

This explains why the connection doesn't get closed with the GOAWAY error: the client is not sending keepalives correctly. This is triggering this code: https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/d0f0aac905c7e9060b14a3ef438f991077376ac2/src/core/ext/transport/chttp2/transport/writing.cc#L67

I found this as part of my [investigation of gRPC client keepalive misconfigurations](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/25713). I was curious why I only saw this with Go clients.

Here is the raw output from `GRPC_TRACE=http GRPC_VERBOSITY=debug`, with some unnecessary lines removed:
